WESTMEATH COUNTY COUNCIL Local Authority Development - File Ref. LAA2-2026 
 
Nature and Extent of Development: 
The development of a walking and cycling path connecting the Ballinahown Sports park to 
Bórd na Móna Lands at Ballinahown, Co. Westmeath. The works will include the following: 
 
Construction of a 1.3km, 3m wide paved pedestrian and cycleway. 
 
Provision of associated Drainage works. 
 
Erection of new boundary fences, entrances, and hedges. 
 
Construction of a pedestrian and cycleway bridge. 
 
Signage map boards, tourist information and public lighting where required. 
 
Cycle parking facilities i.e. benches, cycle stands etc. 
 
Dear Cathaoirleach and Members,  
 
Please see below, Planning Report in accordance with Section 179 of the Planning and 
Development Act 2000 (as amended) and Part 8 of the Planning and Development Regulations 
2001 (as amended). 
 
Project Background 
Westmeath County Council’s Athlone Moate Municipal District has proposed a Part 8 planning 
project to develop a 1.3km walking and cycling linkage from the Ballinahown Sports Park to 
Bórd na Móna Lands at Ballinahown, Co. Westmeath.  
The project involves the creation of a walking and cycling path connecting the Ballinahown 
Sports park to Bórd na Móna Lands at Ballinahown, Co. Westmeath. The proposed 
development will include the following:

Section 1 
1.0 
Site Overview  
The application site is located within the village of Ballinahown. The proposed development 
will consist of a pedestrian and cycle link from Ballinahown Village to Bórd na Móna lands at 
Ballinahown. The proposed greenway a 1.3 km combined pedestrian and cycleway extending 
from Ballinahown Sports Park onto adjoining lands predominantly in agricultural use, located 
west of the L-1406 local road in Ballinahown, Co. Westmeath. Within close proximity to the 
proposed greenway is the National Monument WM035-009---- Bullaun stone.  The subject 
lands are not located within or immediately adjacent to any European Site (designated 
SAC/SPA).

1.1  Origins of Proposal and Funding of Works 
The project is proposed to be undertaken by Westmeath County Council, financed through a 
combination of Council funds and government grant support. The project forms part of a 
wider strategy to integrate Ballinahown village with the emerging Greenway network, by 
providing a dedicated pedestrian and cycle connection to the planned Bórd na Móna 
Greenway linking Athlone to Clonmacnoise. The proposed scheme will also improve access to 
Greenway amenities for residents of Ballinahown and the wider hinterland, who, despite 
living in close proximity to these recreational assets, currently experience limited safe and 
convenient access.

1.6 Policy Context  
1.6.1 National & Regional Policy Context 
Project Ireland 2040 - Revised National Planning Framework – April 2025 (NPF) 
The National Planning Framework (NPF) sets out a high-level, long-term strategic plan for 
shaping the future growth and sustainable development of Ireland to the year 2040. It is 
underpinned by ten National Strategic Outcomes (NSOs), which reflect the overarching vision 
for balanced regional development, environmental sustainability, economic competitiveness, 
and quality of life. These are supported by a series of more detailed National Policy Objectives 
(NPOs), which guide decision-making at national, regional, and local levels.

Page 6 of 18 
 
     PART 8 LAA (2-2026) WESTMEATH COUNTY COUNCIL – Ballinahown Greenway 
The National Planning Framework (NPF) emphasises the importance of reducing reliance on 
private cars by promoting the development of high-quality walking and cycling infrastructure. 
This approach aims to support healthier, more active lifestyles and to foster more sustainable, 
accessible, and liveable urban environments. 
In the context of the proposed project, the following NPOs are particularly relevant: 
 
National Policy Objective 37: seeks to ensure the integration of safe and convenient 
alternatives to the car into the design of communities. It specifically prioritises walking and 
cycling access to both existing and proposed developments, ensuring that active travel is a 
viable and appealing option for people of all ages. 
National Policy Objective 93: promotes integrated spatial planning that supports walking and 
cycling as preferred modes of transport. The objective links active travel infrastructure with 
broader goals of improving air quality and reducing exposure to pollution, recognising the role 
of walking and cycling in creating healthier and more environmentally sustainable 
communities. 
 
Project Ireland 2040 - National Development Plan (NDP) 
The NDP emphasises the need to provide “safe alternative active travel options such as 
segregated cycling and walking facilities can also help alleviate congestion and meet climate 
action objectives by providing viable alternatives and connectivity with existing public 
transport infrastructure”. The NDP encourage a significant “modal shift through greater levels 
of investment and further development of meaningful alternatives to private car uses, such 
as new urban cycling and walking routes which will provide additional sustainable travel 
options.” 
 
Regional Spatial and Economic Strategy for the Eastern and Midland Region (2019-2031)  
The Regional Spatial and Economic Strategy (RSES) for the Eastern and Midland Region 
provides a long-term, statutory framework to implement Project Ireland 2040, integrating 
both the National Planning Framework (NPF) and the National Development Plan (NDP). It 
focuses on coordinated spatial planning, sustainable economic development, climate action, 
and alignment of infrastructure investment across the region.

Page 7 of 18

The RSES promotes healthy placemaking and recognises the importance of active travel 
measures to bring about behavioural changes and more sustainable transport use. In this 
regard, it is recognised that the provision of cycleways can enhance areas, contributing to 
more attractive places and create opportunities to be physically active and reduce the 
negative consequences of car-based commuting. 
It is a Regional Policy Objective that Local authorities seek to support the planned provision 
of easily accessible social, community, cultural and recreational facilities and ensure that all 
communities have access to a range of facilities that meet the needs of the communities they 
serve (RPO 9.14). 
 
Climate Action Plan 2025 
The Climate Action Plan supports the transition to a net zero carbon society and promotes 
sustainable travel through expanded walking, cycling, and public transport infrastructure. 
Relevant measures include Action TR/25/7, which commits to advancing the rollout of walking 
and cycling infrastructure in line with the National Cycle Network and Cycle Connects plans. 
 
1.6.2 Local Policy Context 
Westmeath County Development Plan 2021-2027 (WCDP) 
The proposed cycle and footpath in Ballinahown directly supports the overarching aim of the 
Westmeath County Development Plan to achieve a sustainable, integrated, and low-carbon 
transport system with excellent connectivity by enhancing existing transport infrastructure to 
facilitate safer and more convenient active travel. 
Specifically: 
• 
Integration of land use and transport (CPO 2.16): The proposal prioritises cycling and 
walking through segregated cycle tracks, footpaths, and shared crossings, promoting 
active travel as a viable mode of transport. 
• 
Promotion of sustainable transport and walkable communities (CPO 7.3 & CPO 10.2): 
By providing safe, accessible, and direct routes for pedestrians and cyclists, the 
scheme encourages modal shift away from private cars, making everyday facilities and 
services within short walking or cycling distances. 
• 
Health, safety, and environmental benefits (CPO 10.11 & CPO 10.15): The 
development includes safe, direct, and convenient cycle routes and footpaths, with 
physical separation from vehicular traffic, enhancing the streetscape for pedestrians, 
cyclists, and people with reduced mobility.

• 
Design standards and best practice (CPO 10.13): All cycle and pedestrian infrastructure 
is proposed in line with the National Cycle Manual, the Design Manual for Urban Roads 
and Streets, and international best practice, ensuring high-quality, future-proof active 
travel provision. 
1.7 Siting and Design  
The proposed development extends for approximately 1.3 kilometres in length and is located 
within and adjoining the village of Ballinahown, County Westmeath. The route commences at 
the L-1406 local road within Ballinahown Sports Park, adjacent to Ballinahown National 
School, where it runs parallel to the Sports Park for a distance of approximately 200 metres. 
From this point, the route continues in a generally north-westerly direction, crossing an 
existing drainage channel via a proposed pedestrian and cycle bridge, before traversing 
agricultural lands for a distance of approximately 1.1 kilometres to its western terminus 
within the Bórd na Móna lands. 
The entirety of the scheme will be constructed off-road, following a predominantly westerly 
alignment from Ballinahown village towards the Bórd na Móna lands. The total land area 
associated with the development is approximately 1.2 hectares 
The proposed works include  
 Construction of a 3m wide paved pedestrian and cycleway. 
 
Provision of associated Drainage works. 
 
Erection of new boundary fences, entrances, and hedges. 
 
Construction of a pedestrian and cycleway bridge. 
 
Signage Map boards, tourist information and Public Lighting where required. 
 
Cycle parking facilities i.e. benches, cycle stands etc. 
 
1.8  Heritage and Archaeological Impacts 
The settlement of Ballinahown has an attractive and distinctive built form. The proposed 
development does not impact any protected structures or ACA. The proposed path is located 
within 50m of a - National Monument WM035-009---- Bullaun stone.   
An appropriately qualified Archaeologist will be engaged to undertake an investigation of the 
site and undertake preliminary test pits and to oversee the site construction works.

1.9 Services Provision 
No water and foul water connections are required as part of this development. 
 
1.10 Appropriate Assessment 
Appropriate Assessment is now a standard legal requirement or all plans and projects likely 
to have a significant impact on European sites i.e. Special Areas of Conservation (SAC) or 
Special Protection Areas (SPA). A Stage 1 Appropriate Assessment (AA) Screening Report for 
the proposed works was undertaken by ORS Consultants.  
There are an identified 13(no.) designated Natura 2000 sites situated within a 15km radius of 
the proposed site and 4(no.) with potential indirect linkages. The development works 
proposed are not required for the nature conservation management of these sites. It is noted 
that the conservation objectives for the SACs and SPAs in the vicinity are to maintain or 
restore favourable conservation condition of habitats and species listed as Special 
Conservation Interests for which the SPA/SAC has been selected.  
 
Map 1: Natura 2000 Sites in proximity to proposal. 
There are no Natura 2000 sites in close proximity and no hydrological connectivity between 
the development site area and these SPA/SAC sites. Having regard to the narrow footprint of

Page 10 of 18 
 
     PART 8 LAA (2-2026) WESTMEATH COUNTY COUNCIL – Ballinahown Greenway 
the proposed Greenway Path within the rural/agricultural enirons of Ballinahown - and in 
considering the content of the Stage 1 Screening for Appropriate Assessment prepared by 
ORS; it is considered that there is no potential source-pathway-receptor links to any of the 
Natura 2000 sites mapped in Map 1 above, or other Natura sites outside of this 15km defined 
area. There are no potential for impacts arising from the construction or operation phase of 
the project to give rise to impacts on water quality of any Natura 2000 sites within the zone 
of influence of the project. Given the absence of impact pathways or potential for interactions 
between the project and any Natura 2000 sites, there will be no potential for the project to 
result in any significant effects to any Natura 2000 sites. 
Relationship with other Relevant Plans and Programmes  
The site of the proposed development is located in the Ballinahown Village settlement, a 
designated rural node in the Westmeath County Development Plan 2021-2027.  
An Appropriate Assessment for this Plan was carried out and concluded that, mitigation 
measures identified are adequate to ensure that the integrity of site in the Natura 2000 
network will not be adversely affected as a result of potential impacts of the policies 
contained within the Plan and with the inclusion of relevant mitigating policies in the Plan, 
there is no potential for significant effects either alone or in combination with other plans.   
However, all individual plans/projects must also be considered for their compliance with 
Article 6(3) of the Habitats Directive on a case-by-case basis. 
It is considered that having regard to the siting of the proposed development from the SPAs 
and SACs (illustrated at Map 1 above), that the proposal would not give rise to any significant 
adverse direct, indirect or secondary impacts on the integrity of any nearby Natura 2000 sites 
having regard to the nature of the proposed development and separation distances to 
adjoining Natura 2000 sites.  
Having regard to the characteristics of the proposed development, the nature and distance 
of the potential impact pathways, and the separation from designated European sites, it is 
concluded that there is no likelihood of significant effects on the Qualifying Interests, Special 
Conservation Interests, or the Conservation Objectives of any Natura 2000 site. 
The AA Screening Report was referred to the Council’s Environment Section, who raised no 
objections to the conclusion of the AASR.   
 
1.11 Environmental Impact Assessment  
The proposed development does not fall within the mandatory requirement for an EIA as 
addressed in EU Directive 85/337/EEC (as amended by Directive 97/11/EC).  
An Environmental Impact Assessment Screening exercise was undertaken as part of the pre-
assessment determination. The screening report determined there is no real likelihood of 
significant effects on the environment arising from the proposed development of the

Page 11 of 18 
 
     PART 8 LAA (2-2026) WESTMEATH COUNTY COUNCIL – Ballinahown Greenway 
Ballinahown Greenway (a 1.3 km combined pedestrian and cycleway from Ballinahown Sports 
Park through lands predominantly in agricultural use, located to the west of the L-1406 local 
road in Ballinahown, Co. Westmeath) and an Environmental Impact Assessment is not 
required in this instance. 
Having regard to the information presented for the development in the plan proposals, it is 
reasonable to conclude that there is no real likelihood of significant effects on the 
environment arising from the proposed development and a full Environmental Impact 
Assessment is not required.  
Section 2 
2.0 Internal Section Reports and Prescribed Bodies Submissions 
2.1 Internal Sections Reports Received 
Environment Section 
Report received on 19 June 2026.  The report advises that they have reviewed the AA 
Screening Assessment carried out by ORS Consultants. It is identified that the AA report 
considered the proposed development and impacts on all European Sites within the identified 
zone of influence (15km and beyond). The screening report recommended that the significant 
effects individually or in combination with other plans and project could be excluded and the 
report concluded that this development has been screened out from proceeding to a stage 2 
report.  
The Environment Section concur with the AA Screening conclusion and have no objection to 
the screening determination. 
The report recommends the following matters to be included: 
1. Prior to a commencement notice being issued the applicant shall submit a 
Construction & Environmental Management Plan (CEMP) for the construction phase. 
This Plan shall provide the environmental management framework to be adhered to 
during the pre-commencement, construction and operational phases of the proposed 
development and it shall incorporate the mitigating principles to ensure that the work 
is carried out in a way that minimises the potential for any environmental impacts to 
occur. It shall contain at minimum: introduction, site and project details, surface/ 
ground water protection, dust control, noise and vibration, construction phase waste 
management, vermin control, roles and responsibilities, emergency response, 
mitigation proposals, compliance, and review (not exhaustive). 
2. The applicant shall submit a Construction and Demolition Resource Waste 
Management Plan (RWMP) as set out in the Best Practice Guidelines for the 
'Preparation of Resource and Waste Management Plans for C & D Projects (2021)' 
including demonstration of proposals to adhere to best practice and protocols. The

Page 12 of 18 
 
     PART 8 LAA (2-2026) WESTMEATH COUNTY COUNCIL – Ballinahown Greenway 
updated RWMP shall include specific proposals as to how the RWMP will be measured 
and monitored for effectiveness; these details shall be placed on the file and retained 
as part of the public record. The updated RWMP must be submitted to the planning 
authority for written agreement prior to the commencement of the development. All 
records (including for waste and all resources) pursuant to the agreed RWMP shall 
always be maintained and kept live and made available for inspection at the office. 
3. All oils and hydrocarbons are to be stored in a bunded area. The bund shall be 
designed in accordance with BS: 8007: 1987 a code of practice for the design of 
concrete for retaining aqueous liquids. 
4. Adequate provision (including access and suitable receptacle storage space) should be 
incorporated into the scheme design to accommodate four separate waste collection 
of recyclable, food, glass, and residual waste streams. 
5. Dust deposition from the construction works should not exceed 350mg/sq.m/day 
(based on a 30-day composite sample) as measured using the Bergerhoff Method, or 
130mg/sq.m/day as measured on a “Frisbee” type dust gauge beyond the boundary 
of the site. Dust monitoring location shall be agreed with Westmeath County Council. 
6. There should be no discharge of contaminated water to any surface water drainage 
system or surface water course.  
7. The applicant shall ensure that activities at the site, during the construction stage shall 
not give rise to noise levels off site which exceed the following sound pressure limits 
(Leq: 30 minutes) beyond the site boundary.  
Day-time (8.00am to 8.00pm) 55dB(A) 
Night-time (8.00pm to 8.00am) 45dB(A) 
In addition, noise levels measured at noise sensitive locations in the vicinity of the site 
shall not exceed a level of 10 dB(A) above existing noise levels during core working 
hours, and 5 dB(A) at any other time. All noise measurements shall be carried and 
assessed in accordance with Environmental Protection Agency Guidance Note for 
Noise: Licence Applications, Surveys and Assessments in Relation to Scheduled 
Activities (NG4). Noise sensitive locations shall be agreed with Westmeath County 
Council.

Uisce Éireann: 
Report received 16 June 2026. The report confirms that the applicant has not included a

Department of Housing, Local Government and Heritage 
Report received 19 June 2026. The report advises that the proposed development is located 
within close proximity to Recorded Monument WM035-009---- : Bullaun stone, which is 
subject to statutory protection in the Record of Monuments and Places, established under 
section 12 of the National Monuments (Amendment) Act 1994. 
Given the extent and location of the proposed development, it could impact on subsurface 
archaeological remains. In line with national policy, see Section 3.6 of Framework and 
Principles for the Protection of the Archaeological Heritage 1999, the Department 
recommends 
that 
an 
Archaeological 
Impact 
Assessment/further 
archaeological 
assessment/investigation, as described below, should be prepared to assess the impact on 
the archaeological heritage. This assessment should be submitted as Further Information 
prior to any grant of planning. This will enable the Planning Authority and this office to 
prepare an informed archaeological recommendation before a planning decision is taken. 
Archaeological Impact Assessment: 
1. The applicant is required to engage the services of a suitably qualified archaeologist to 
carry out an archaeological assessment of the development site, in relation to 
Recorded Monument WM035-009---- : Bullaun stone. No sub-surface work should be 
undertaken until an archaeological assessment has been completed and commented 
on by this office. 
2. The archaeologist should carry out any relevant documentary research and inspect the 
development site. This assessment shall also define a buffer area or area contiguous 
with the monument which will preserve the setting and visual amenity of the site. No 
sub-surface work should be undertaken in the absence of the archaeologist without 
his/her express consent. 
3.  A programme of test excavation shall be carried out at locations chosen by the 
archaeologist (licensed under the National Monuments Acts 1930-2004), having 
consulted the site drawings and the Department of Housing, Local Government & 
Heritage. 
4. Having completed the work, the archaeologist should submit a written report stating 
their recommendations to the Department of Housing, Local Government & Heritage. 
Where archaeological material/features are shown to be present, preservation in situ, 
preservation by record (excavation) or monitoring may be required.

2.3 Chief Executive Response 
The content of the submissions from the internal Departments and Prescribed Bodies are 
acknowledged 
and 
welcomed. 
Following 
consideration 
of 
the 
matters 
raised 
recommendations are set out below where appropriate.  
The recommendation received from the Environment Section is noted and constitutes 
standard operational procedures associated with a development of this type. It is noted that 
a CEMP and RWMP were both submitted with the project documentation. Having regard to 
the content of same, it is not considered that any amendment to the proposed construction 
methodology is necessary in this instance.   
In respect of the report from Uisce Éireann it is confirmed that the proposed development 
does not include a new water or wastewater connection and no adverse impact on Uisce 
Éireann infrastructure is anticipated. The scheme consists principally of a pedestrian and cycle 
link with associated bridges, drainage works and ancillary infrastructure. The CEMP includes 
extensive measures for the protection of surface water and groundwater including pollution 
prevention measures, drainage controls, fuel and chemical storage requirements, spill 
response procedures, silt controls and protection of existing drainage channels. The proposed 
bridge crossings will be constructed without in-stream works.  
In respect of the submission from the Department of Housing, Local Government and 
Heritage, the archaeological sensitivity of the site is acknowledged and this was referenced in 
the project documentation. The proposed Archaeological Impact Assessment is considered 
appropriate given the proximity of the Recorded Monument WM035-009---- : Bullaun stone. 
It is recommended that there would be consultation with the National Monuments Service 
and the appointment of a suitably qualified archaeologist to undertake archaeological 
monitoring and any further assessment deemed necessary prior to and during construction. 
The appointed archaeologist shall carry out an archaeological assessment of the site, monitor 
the works on site and liaise with the Department of Housing, Local Government and Heritage 
in the event that any archaeological material is discovered during Archaeological Testing.

Submission Ref No. WM-C146-2 
Submission received from Colm Ryder (Irish Cycling Campaign) on the 19/06/2026 broadly 
supporting the development. The Irish Cycling Campaign welcomes the proposed 
development and supports the provision of a 3.0m wide shared pedestrian and cycle facility. 
The submission seeks further context regarding the purpose of the scheme, its connection to 
the Bord na Móna lands, and how the project fits within the wider Greenway network and 
active travel strategy. 
Chief Executive Response. 
The submission and the comments made are noted and acknowledged. The proposed scheme 
is intended to provide a safe, off-road pedestrian and cycling connection between 
Ballinahown Village and the planned Bórd na Móna Greenway lands. The project forms part 
of the Council's wider strategy to improve connectivity between rural communities and the 
emerging Greenway network, thereby promoting active travel, recreation, tourism and 
sustainable transport opportunities. 
At its western terminus, the scheme will connect to the Bórd na Móna Greenway currently 
under construction, which will provide links to both Athlone and Clonmacnoise. As a result, 
the proposed 1.3km route will form part of an off-road recreational and active travel corridor 
of approximately 15km in length. The route has the potential to attract users from 
Ballinahown to Athlone and Clonmacnoise, while also encouraging visitors and day-trippers 
travelling on the Greenway network to visit Ballinahown Village. 
The project has been developed to address the current lack of safe and convenient access 
from Ballinahown Village to the future Greenway network. The route will connect 
Ballinahown Sports Park, the village and surrounding hinterland directly to the planned Bórd 
na Móna Greenway corridor, which is intended to form part of the wider Athlone–
Clonmacnoise Greenway.  
In addition, both Westmeath County Council and Offaly County Council continue to explore 
opportunities for further connections to the wider cycling and greenway network, including 
links to the Old Rail Trail Greenway and the Grand Canal Greenway. The Council considers 
that the provision of this strategic link will ensure that local residents can fully benefit from 
planned Greenway investment in the area and will improve accessibility to recreational and 
active travel infrastructure for people of all ages and abilities.

Section 4 
4.0 Conclusion 
Having considered the plans and particulars, together with the reports and submissions 
received in association with the development proposal, it is considered that the development 
is consistent with national, regional, and local policy (Westmeath County Development Plan 
2021-2027) and as such is in accordance with the proper planning and sustainable 
development of the area.  
Having regard to the content of the submissions received from prescribed bodies and the 
public, and subject to the recommendations set out below, it is considered that the proposed 
development which consists of 1.3km greenway walking and cycling link between 
Ballinahown Sports Park to Bórd Na Mona Lands at Ballinahown, Co. Westmeath and 
therefore 
- 
Would not seriously injure the amenities of the area or of property in the vicinity. 
- 
Would not negatively impact the archaeological and natural heritage in the vicinity. 
- 
Would not be prejudicial to public health.  
- 
Would be acceptable in terms of traffic safety and convenience.  
- 
Would provide an accessible community facility.  
- 
Would improve the provision of cycle and walking routes in the local area and provide 
opportunities to link into other local and regional projects. 
 
4.1 Recommendation 
Having regard to the above, it is considered that the proposal will deliver a greenway link with 
walking and cycling facilities and help to strengthen and develop the future Athlone to 
Clonmacnoise greenway and link into other greenway projects locally. The development is 
consistent with the provisions of the Westmeath County Development Plan 2021-2027 and 
as such is in accordance with the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. 
Accordingly, it is recommended that the development proceeds in accordance with the 
scheme documentation and the following amendments/modifications:

Amendments: 
1. Archaeology: 
a) An appropriately qualified and experienced archaeologist shall be engaged for the 
duration of the project to carry out an archaeological assessment of the development 
site, in relation to Recorded Monument WM035-009----: Bullaun stone. No sub-
surface work should be undertaken until an archaeological assessment has been 
completed and submitted for the written approval of the Planning Authority. 
 
b) The appointed archaeologist shall carry out any relevant documentary research and 
inspect the development site. This assessment shall also define a buffer area or area 
contiguous with the monument which will preserve the setting and visual amenity of 
the site. No sub-surface work should be undertaken in the absence of the 
archaeologist without his/her express consent. 
 
c) A programme of test excavation shall be carried out at locations chosen by the 
archaeologist (licensed under the National Monuments Acts 1930-2004), having 
consulted the site drawings and the Department of Housing, Local Government & 
Heritage. 
 
d) Having completed the work, the archaeologist shall submit a written report stating 
their recommendations to the Department of Housing, Local Government & Heritage 
and the Planning Authority. Where archaeological material/features are shown to be 
present, preservation in situ, preservation by record (excavation) or monitoring may 
be required.
